message.content: In lions, the most striking example of a dominant genetic trait is the **presence of a mane in adult male lions**. This trait is governed by genes that influence hair growth and pigmentation, and it is expressed in males while females lack a mane. The underlying genetics involve the androgen receptor pathway, which is activated by testosterone and leads to the development of the mane’s dense, dark fur. This dominant expression is why you see a mane in virtually all adult male lions but not in females.
